title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint
Low back pain.

HPI
The patient is a 50-year-old male presenting for evaluation of persistent low back pain. He reports a dull, aching sensation in his lumbar region that has persisted for approximately three weeks. He notes that the pain is exacerbated by prolonged sitting and heavy lifting but is partially relieved by rest and heat application. He denies any radiating pain into the lower extremities, numbness, tingling, or weakness. He denies any recent falls or acute trauma to the spine.

Medication List
Multivitamin daily.

Exam
The patient is alert and in no acute distress. He is upright and moving comfortably. Physical examination of the lumbar spine reveals mild tenderness to palpation over the paraspinal muscles. Range of motion is limited by discomfort but remains within functional limits. There are no neurological deficits noted in the lower extremities; strength and sensation are intact.

Assessment
Low back pain.

Plan
The patient will begin a regimen of stretching exercises and heat therapy. He was advised on proper body mechanics and ergonomic adjustments for his workspace. Follow-up is scheduled in four weeks if symptoms persist or worsen.

Problem List
- Chronic systolic heart failure
- Status post appendectomy
- Status post cholecystectomy

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: Heart failure appears only in a problem list and is not addressed in this encounter, so it is not supported for this date of service.

distractors.why: A problem-list entry alone does not show the condition affected care at this visit.
